questions.q: What are the five qualities that make a gem?
choices: Beauty, rarity, durability, value and acceptability
Colour, weight, size, price and origin
Hardness, toughness, stability, luster and density
Rarity, fashion, size, fire and colour
questions.why: A stone becomes a gem when it brings together these five qualities.

choices: a real red corundum, made by people
questions.why: A synthetic gem has the same composition and the same structure as the natural gem.

questions.q: Opal is a gem that is…
questions.why: Opal and obsidian have no regular order: they are amorphous.

questions.q: What are the three components of durability?
questions.why: Scratches, blows, environment: three ways to hold up over time.

choices: gems with no counterpart in nature
questions.why: They are several pieces glued together.

questions.q: What does the law say about the international trade in elephant ivory?
choices: It is free everywhere in the world
It is only banned for mammoth
It is allowed with a simple sales certificate
questions.why: Acceptability is also a matter of law: a seller must prove the origin of the material.

questions.q: What are gems “with no counterpart in nature”?
choices: Gems too rare to be sold
Gems that do not exist naturally, like YAG or cubic zirconia
questions.why: They are made by people and have no natural equivalent.

questions.q: Which of these materials is of organic origin?
questions.why: Pearls, amber, coral and jet are produced by living beings.

questions.q: What is a gemmologist mainly for?
choices: To recognize the species, spot treatments and imitations, and check quality
To extract stones from the mine
questions.why: The qualities of a stone are not guessed: they are measured.

choices: where diamonds come from, so that they are not conflict diamonds
questions.why: Conflict diamonds are banned from trade.
